sn45.21:1.2: “Wrong way” is _micchattā_, literally “wrongness”. | The roots of both _sammā_ (Sanskrit _samyak_) and _micchā_ (Sanskrit _mithyā_) convey a similar sense of “together”, but _sammā_ implied harmonious union (Rig Veda 4.58.6, 5.9.5, 9.73.2), while _micchā_ was associated with contention or clashing (1.119.3, 1.144.3, 6.25.2). Over time, _micchā_ came to convey “wrong, false, vain, mistaken”, while _sammā_ was “right, harmonious, integrated”.
